verdict.rationale: Omarchy's first-party docs say it ships OpenCode and Claude Code as the default agent harnesses. They document terminal aliases (`c` for OpenCode, `cx` for Claude Code in danger mode) and pre-wired launchers for every major coding-agent CLI, and first boot invites the user to set up a default agent. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the bundled agents write and run code in the terminal.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can use built-in AI coding agents directly in the terminal to write and run code

citations.quote: Omarchy ships with [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/) and [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) as the default agent harnesses for programmers.
invoke the `c` alias to start OpenCode within that directory. Claude Code ... can be started in danger mode using the `cx` alias.
Omarchy ships pre-wired lazy-loaded launchers for every major coding-agent CLI.
